title: Enigma raises $70M to make controlling a robot as easy as adjusting the volume
slides: Can adjusting a volume knob truly control a robot?
Enigma raised $70M for a universal robotic interface.
The interface works on any robot, regardless of software.
Now you script robots via a simple dial, not code.
Test Enigma's SDK today—your first task sets the dial.
thread_text:
1. A dial for robots?

Enigma raised $70M to let you control any robot with a volume knob, no code needed.

2. Universal interface

The hardware works on any robot, regardless of its operating system or software stack.

3. No programming required

Instead of scripting, you twist a dial to set tasks—speed, direction, or sequence.

4. From knob to control

This turns physical interaction into robot commands, bypassing traditional programming barriers.

5. Try it yourself

Download Enigma's SDK today and complete your first task using just the dial—no coding required.

script: Turn a knob to command any robot.
Their interface works on every robot.
You script robots with a simple dial.

instagram.caption:
You could soon control a robot with the same motion you use to turn up the volume on a speaker. 🎛️

Enigma just raised $70 million for a universal hardware dial that works with any robot, no matter its operating system. Instead of writing code, you twist a physical knob to set the machine’s speed, direction, or sequence. 🦾

For someone who creates content or prototypes, this means programming a robot arm for a shoot or an assembly could become a two-second twist instead of a 30-minute script. 🎬

What’s the first task you’d map to a simple dial on your gear?
